[RLOW.4.6.1] **`cooldown T` lowers to a `RuleCooldown` atom and a rate gate.** For a
rule whose header carries `cooldown T`, the compiler must emit a `RuleCooldown` atom
carrying the window ([RDSC.6.5]) and a rate gate in the terminal's
`fire_guard` ([RDSC.4a.8.2.1]): a call of `FN_RATE_ALLOW` whose arguments are
the rule's name, the activation key's values ([RLOW.4.6.2.3]) in that key's
order, each a `VarExpr` read of its pattern's fact ([RLOW.6.3.1]), and the
window in nanoseconds. The runtime evaluates the gate once per firing
([RDSC.4a.8.2.3]) against the state [RLOW.4.6.2.1] defines.

The compiler emits the gate **only** when the rule carries `cooldown`. A
`cooldown` does not change how the clock re-drives the rule ([LTIM.2.4.2]).
Where the rule also has a condition in its fire guard, the guard is their
conjunction, the condition left and the rate gate right ([RDSC.4a.8.2.1]), so
the runtime evaluates the gate only once the condition holds.
